alternatingKneeRaises.title: Alternating knee raises
alternatingKneeRaises.description: Raise knees toward chest alternately to engage core and hip flexors.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart
Raise one knee toward your chest
Lower it back down with control
Alternate legs in a steady rhythm

hammerCurls.title: Alternating hammer curls
hammerCurls.description: Alternate arms to strengthen biceps and forearms.
instructions: Hold weights with palms facing each other
Keep elbows close to your sides
Curl one weight up toward your shoulder
Lower with control and alternate arms

lateralRaises.title: Lateral raises
lateralRaises.description: Lift both arms to target shoulders with control.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Hold weights at your sides with palms facing in
Raise both arms out to the sides to shoulder height
Lower slowly back to starting position

calfRaises.title: Calf raises
calfRaises.description: Rise onto your toes to strengthen calves and ankles.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart
Rise up onto the balls of your feet
Hold at the top for a moment
Lower back down with control

lunges.title: Lunges
lunges.description: Step forward, lower with control, and drive through the front heel.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart
Step forward with one leg
Lower your hips until both knees are bent at 90 degrees
Push back to starting position and alternate legs

pushups.title: Push-ups
pushups.description: Control your core and chest through each rep.
instructions: Start in plank position with hands shoulder-width apart
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels
Lower your chest toward the ground with control
Push back up to starting position

squats.title: Squats
squats.description: Drive through your heels to stabilize hips and knees.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Lower your hips back and down as if sitting
Keep chest up and knees tracking over toes
Drive through heels to return to standing

standingLegRaises.title: Standing leg raises
standingLegRaises.description: Lift one leg laterally to strengthen hip abductors and improve balance.
instructions: Stand with feet together
Lift one leg out to the side, keeping it straight
Hold for a moment at the top
Lower with control and alternate legs

standingChestFly.title: Standing chest fly
standingChestFly.description: Bring arms together with bent elbows to engage chest and shoulders.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
Hold weights at chest height with elbows slightly bent
Open arms wide to the sides
Bring arms back together in front of your chest

mediapipe.title: How Pose Detection Works
mediapipe.description: Understand how AI detects your body movements and counts repetitions accurately
mediapipe.intro: Pose detection is an advanced AI technology that tracks your body movements in real-time using your device's camera. It identifies 33 key points on your body to analyze your exercise form and count repetitions automatically.

howItWorks.title: How Does It Work?
howItWorks.description: The system uses computer vision to detect and track body landmarks:

steps.1: The camera captures your movements in real-time
steps.2: AI identifies 33 body points (shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, etc.)
steps.3: The app calculates angles between joints to analyze movement
steps.4: When you complete a full range of motion, a repetition is counted

positioning.title: Positioning Your Device
positioning.subtitle: Proper camera placement is essential for accurate tracking

mobile.title: Mobile Device
mobile.description: Place your phone on a stable surface or tripod at chest height, 6-8 feet away. Ensure your entire body is visible in the frame.

laptop.title: Laptop/Webcam
laptop.description: Position your laptop or external webcam at chest to head height. Step back until your full body fits in the frame (head to feet).

privacy.title: Your Privacy is Protected
privacy.description: All pose detection happens directly on your device. No videos or images are sent to external servers. Your workout data stays completely private and secure.

distance.title: Optimal Camera Distance
distance.description: Stand 6-8 feet (2-2.5 meters) away from your device. Your entire body should be visible in the frame from head to feet. Too close and the camera can't see your full movement; too far and detection becomes less accurate.

positioning.title: Body Positioning
positioning.description: Position yourself so your full body is visible. For exercises like squats or push-ups, ensure your head, torso, arms, and legs are all in frame. Turn sideways for better tracking of depth movements (like squats).

lighting.title: Good Lighting
lighting.description: Exercise in a well-lit area. Natural light works best, but avoid direct sunlight or backlighting that creates shadows. The AI needs to clearly see your body outline and joints.

clothing.title: Wear Fitted Clothing
clothing.description: Wear form-fitting athletic wear. Baggy clothes can hide your body's movements and make it harder for the system to track joint positions accurately.

background.title: Clear Background
background.description: Choose a plain, uncluttered background. Avoid mirrors, busy patterns, or other people in the frame. A simple wall or open space works best for clear body detection.

movement.title: Smooth, Controlled Movements
movement.description: Perform exercises with deliberate, controlled movements. Going too fast can cause the AI to miss the full range of motion. Quality over speed ensures accurate rep counting.

1.solution: Ensure you're completing the full range of motion. Move slowly and deliberately through each rep. Check that your entire body is visible in the frame.

2.solution: Improve lighting conditions and move to a clearer background. Make sure you're at the right distance (6-8 feet) from the camera.

3.solution: Wear more fitted clothing and ensure good lighting. Avoid positions where your body parts overlap or are hidden from the camera's view.

4.problem: Counting extra reps or skipping reps
4.solution: Slow down your movements and ensure each rep has a clear starting and ending position. Avoid bouncing or partial reps.

5.problem: Camera not activating or showing permission error
5.mobileSolution: Go to Settings > WorkoutPilot > Permissions and enable camera access.
5.webSolution: When the browser requests camera access, select 'Allow'. If you already blocked it, click the lock/camera icon in the address bar and change the camera permission to 'Allow'.

exercises.title: Exercise Execution Guide
exercises.description: Master proper form and maximize rep counting accuracy for all exercises
exercises.intro: Proper exercise execution is crucial for both your safety and accurate rep counting. This guide will help you understand how to perform exercises correctly so the system can track your movements effectively.

repCounting.title: How Reps Are Counted
repCounting.description: The system counts repetitions by analyzing joint angles and movement patterns:

steps.1: The starting position is detected (e.g., standing upright for squats, arms extended for push-ups)
steps.2: You move through the full range of motion to the bottom position
steps.3: You return to the starting position - this completes one repetition

visibility.title: Keep All Body Parts Visible
visibility.description: Ensure your head, torso, arms, and legs remain in the camera frame throughout the entire exercise. Stepping out of frame will interrupt tracking and may miss counting reps.

tempo.title: Use Controlled Tempo
tempo.description: Perform each repetition with a 2-second descent and 1-second ascent (2-0-1 tempo). This ensures the system has time to analyze your movement and count accurately. Rushing through reps reduces accuracy.

form.title: Maintain Proper Form
form.description: Focus on quality over quantity. Proper form not only prevents injury but also ensures the AI can clearly detect the full range of motion required to count a rep. Partial reps won't be counted.

pauses.title: Pause at End Positions
pauses.description: Briefly pause (0.5-1 second) at the top and bottom of each rep. This gives the system a clear signal that you've completed the movement and helps distinguish between reps.

tips.2: Descend until thighs are parallel to the ground (90-degree knee bend)
tips.3: Keep your chest up and core engaged throughout the movement

tips.3: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels - no sagging hips

tips.2: Raise arms until parallel to the floor (shoulder height)
tips.3: Control the descent - don't let gravity drop your arms

tips.1: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart

tips.3: Alternate legs in a controlled manner, avoid swaying

tips.1: Stand with arms extended, palms facing each other (neutral grip)
tips.2: Bend elbows bringing hands toward shoulders
tips.3: Keep elbows close to your body throughout the movement

tips.3: Lower in a controlled manner until heels almost touch the ground

tips.1: Take a large step forward, keep torso upright
tips.2: Lower until both knees form 90-degree angles
tips.3: Back knee nearly touches ground, front knee over ankle
